summary: Defines managed objects to configure and monitor multicast over IP VPNs supported by MPLS/BGP.

plainLanguage.summary: This is the control panel and dashboard for managing multicast on private network services.

questions: what is the mpls l3vpn multicast mib
what is a pmsi in mpls vpn
which snmp objects monitor multicast vpn
subtitle: An SNMP MIB module for configuring and monitoring multicast over BGP/MPLS Layer 3 VPNs on a provider edge router.

tldr.problem: Operators who run multicast over BGP/MPLS IP VPNs (MVPNs) had no standard, SNMP-readable way to configure or monitor the MVPN state on a Provider Edge (PE) router.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8503 defines the BGP-MPLS-LAYER3-VPN-MULTICAST-MIB module, with scalar objects plus seven tables covering MVPNs, BGP-specific settings, PMSIs, advertisement statistics, multicast routes and next hops, and one notification.
tldr.outcome: A PE can expose its MVPN state and tunable limits through SNMP in a uniform way. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and the module sits at { mib-2 243 }.

today: RFC 8503 is a Proposed Standard and, according to the unit metadata, is not obsoleted or updated by any other RFC. It works alongside the companion MIB in RFC 8502.

sections.title: What This MIB Is For
sections.content:
RFC 6513, RFC 6514 and RFC 6625 specify how to carry multicast over MPLS/BGP Layer 3 Virtual Private Networks. RFC 8503 uses the term MVPN (multicast VPN) for a BGP/MPLS IP VPN that supports multicast.

PE routers attached to an MVPN exchange customer multicast (C-multicast) routing information with each other. RFC 6513 defines two methods: Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM) and BGP. The RFC calls them PIM-MVPN and BGP-MVPN. Most managed objects in the MIB are common to both, and some apply only to BGP-MVPN.
sections.plainLanguage: Some private networks can send one video stream to many offices at once. This document is the list of gauges and switches that lets a network operator watch and adjust that feature.

sections.title: Key Terms: P-tunnels, PMSIs and MVRFs
sections.content:
An MVPN can use various transport mechanisms to carry a packet to all or some PEs across the provider network. These are called provider tunnels (P-tunnels).

A Provider Multicast Service Interface (PMSI) is a conceptual interface instantiated by a P-tunnel. A PE uses it to send customer multicast traffic to all or some PEs in the same VPN. An Inclusive PMSI (I-PMSI) reaches all PEs in the MVPN. A Selective PMSI (S-PMSI) reaches a selected set of them.

As in RFC 4382, each PE keeps one default forwarding table and zero or more VRF tables. A VRF that holds multicast routing information is called an MVRF.
sections.plainLanguage: A PMSI is like a bus route between offices. One kind of route stops at every office, and another kind stops only at the offices that asked for the show.

sections.title: Place in the Management Framework
sections.content:
Managed objects live in a virtual information store called the Management Information Base. They are usually reached through the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) and are defined with the Structure of Management Information (SMI). The module here conforms to SMIv2 (RFC 2578, RFC 2579, RFC 2580).

The module, BGP-MPLS-LAYER3-VPN-MULTICAST-MIB, is meant to be used together with MPLS-L3VPN-STD-MIB (RFC 4382) and IPMCAST-MIB (RFC 5132). It also imports the provider tunnel type from the companion module in RFC 8502.

Its functions are to monitor MVPN attributes on a PE, configure timers and thresholds, notify about creation, deletion and modification of MVRFs, monitor PMSI attributes, monitor advertisement statistics, and monitor multicast routes and their next hops.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIB is one more page in a big binder of standard instruction sheets for network gear. It is meant to be read alongside two other pages in that binder.

sections.title: The Tables
sections.content:
Besides a group of scalars, the module defines seven tables.

  • mvpnGenericTable: one entry per MVPN on a PE. Each entry MUST have a corresponding VRF in MPLS-L3VPN-STD-MIB.
  • mvpnBgpTable: extra information for each BGP-MVPN.
  • mvpnPmsiTable: attributes common to I-PMSIs and S-PMSIs.
  • mvpnSpmsiTable: attributes specific to S-PMSIs. Each S-PMSI here has a matching entry in mvpnPmsiTable.
  • mvpnAdvtStatsTable: statistics about I-PMSI and S-PMSI advertisements sent and received.
  • mvpnMrouteTable: multicast routing information in MVRFs.
  • mvpnMrouteNextHopTable: next hops used to route IP multicast datagrams in MVPNs.

In mvpnGenericTable, an entry records the last action on the MVRF (created, deleted, or a changed I-PMSI or S-PMSI configuration), the protocol used for C-multicast routing (pim or bgp), the Upstream Multicast Hop selection method, and the customer site type (sender and receiver, receiver only, or sender only).
sections.plainLanguage: Think of seven spreadsheets. One lists the private networks, one holds extra facts about those that use BGP, and others track the bus routes, the message counts, the routes and the stops.

sections.title: Scalars and Tunable Limits
sections.content:
The scalar objects count MVRFs on the PE: the total, those for IPv4 and IPv6 C-multicast, those using PIM for IPv4 or IPv6, and those using BGP for IPv4, IPv6 or mLDP C-multicast routing information.

A few objects are read-write and let an operator tune behavior: mvpnSPTunnelLimit (the maximum number of selective provider tunnels for an MVPN on the PE), mvpnBgpCmcastRouteWithdrawalTimer and mvpnBgpSrcSharedTreeJoinTimer (delays for certain C-multicast route advertisements, in milliseconds).

In mvpnBgpTable, read-write objects cap the BGP message rate (mvpnBgpMsgRateLimit, messages per second), the number of S-PMSI A-D routes and their generation frequency, and the number of Source Active A-D routes and their generation frequency.
sections.plainLanguage: Most things in this MIB are gauges you can only read. A few are dials, such as a speed limit on how many messages a router may send each second.

sections.title: PMSI Details, Statistics and the Notification
sections.content:
An entry in mvpnPmsiTable is indexed by the interface index of the PMSI tunnel and records its Route Distinguisher, the tunnel type, and, for PIM tunnels, the group address. The encapsulation type is one of greIp, ipIp or mpls, referring to GRE (RFC 2784), IP-in-IP (RFC 2003) and MPLS (RFC 3032).

The multicast route and next-hop tables report, among other things, the upstream neighbor, expiry times, and packet and octet counters. A next hop is either pruned or forwarding. Counters have companion discontinuity-time objects that say when a counter may have jumped.

The module defines one notification, mvpnMvrfActionTaken. It reports a change in an MVRF on the PE, and the change itself is given by mvpnGenMvrfLastAction.
sections.plainLanguage: The MIB also has a doorbell. When a network is added, removed or changed on the router, the doorbell rings and says what happened.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The module has read-only objects that may be sensitive and read-write objects whose settings change the device's MVPN behavior. Allowing SET operations in a non-secure environment opens devices to attack. The RFC lists each read-write object and how misuse could hurt: for example, abusing the tunnel limit or the BGP rate limits could hurt PE performance or prevent new tunnels or routes.

Address-related objects, such as group, source and peer addresses, may reveal the locations of senders and recipients.

SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security. Implementations SHOULD provide the SNMPv3 security features, and deployment of earlier versions is NOT RECOMMENDED. Implementations claiming SNMPv3 compliance MUST fully support authentication and privacy through the User-based Security Model with the AES cipher.
sections.plainLanguage: Some of these dials could cause trouble if the wrong person turned them, and some gauges show where things are. So only trusted people, over a safe connection, should get to use them.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA assigned the object identifier for the module in the SMI Network Management MGMT Codes Internet-standard MIB registry. The module mvpnMIB (BGP-MPLS-LAYER3-VPN-MULTICAST-MIB) is at { mib-2 243 }.
sections.plainLanguage: The module got its own official number so that no other document uses the same one.
